questions.question: Describe what bones are like and explain why we say bones are alive.
questions.expected_answer: Bones are hard and strong and contain a lot of calcium. Long bones have marrow in the middle that makes blood cells. Bones are alive because they grow as we grow and can heal when they break.

questions.question: What is a joint? Name and describe two kinds of joints, with an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: A joint is where two or more bones meet. A hinge joint, like the knee or elbow, bends in one direction. A ball and socket joint, like the shoulder or hip, can swing in many directions. A fixed joint, like those in the skull, does not move.

questions.question: Explain why the skeleton is called a frame, and give one way that skeletons differ between vertebrates.
questions.expected_answer: The skeleton is many strong bones joined together at joints, like the parts of a frame, and it gives the body shape and holds it up. Skeletons differ: a snake has many ribs but no leg bones, a bird has light bones and wings, and a frog has long back legs for jumping.
